claim: Experts find faults that novices miss: in Johnson 1987 all 5 experts solved both rare-fault generator problems, novices 3/5 and 2/5.
agent_test: Give agent a rare-fault set; compare fault-found rate with and without a recalled-system-model preface at equal tokens.

claim: Experts start from a correct problem space built from the first symptom; novices have no explicit starting picture and search by trial and error.
agent_test: Score whether first hypotheses fall inside the true fault space; compare plain vs forced 'what do symptoms rule out' step.
audit_note: Johnson 1987 supports it for generator/auto technicians; Steinberg and Gitomer only broadly (explicit mental models, physical clues).

claim: In Lesgold et al.'s Sherlock task analysis, the expert solved one sample problem in 7 steps by splitting the suspect space, while one trainee took 14 steps and another 20, tracing circuit paths end to end; the authors say what differs with expertise is which space is split, and Johnson (1995) found strategy type did not separate high from low performers but range of strategies did.
agent_test: Count steps to isolate fault in synthetic circuits; agent with a space-narrowing step vs plain.
audit_note: Lesgold et al. give one expert (7 steps) vs. three trainees (14, 20, others similar) on a single sample problem and say most trainees also try to be systematic by space splitting or sequential tracing; the contrast is not general.
claim_before_audit: Expertise is knowing which space to split, not knowing the split method: experts halve the right space; trainees trace circuits end to end (7 vs 14/20 steps).

claim: In one student study (Johnson et al. 1993, n=34) systems-exam scores did not differ between high and low troubleshooters (19.82 vs 19.88 of 24), suggesting theory knowledge may be a weak predictor of troubleshooting skill; range of strategies (Johnson 1995) and strategic and system knowledge (Katz et al. 1997; Steinberg and Gitomer 1992) were what separated skilled from unskilled technicians.
agent_test: Measure whether adding generic theory text helps; compare with system-specific structure text at equal tokens.
audit_note: The theory-knowledge null comes from one student sample (Johnson et al. 1993, n=34, t(32)=0.073) that the author hedges as 'may not be as important', and a null test is not proof of no prediction.
claim_before_audit: Theory/exam knowledge does not predict troubleshooting skill; range of strategies and system-specific models do.

claim: Strategy type does not separate good from poor troubleshooters; flexibility across strategies does (poor ones are strategy-bound).
agent_test: Test forced strategy switch after N fruitless checks vs fixed strategy.

claim: Premature part swapping and wasteful self-test use mark novices (Frankenstation: swaps without testing 50 control vs 3 tutored vs 8 masters).
agent_test: Count actions taken before the fault is verified; add a 'verify-before-change' guard and compare.
note: Gap search: no component ablation of verify-before-swap exists.

claim: Coached practice on expert-derived task analysis lifts novices to master level on trained tests (about 20 hours; effect 1.27/1.17/0.87 SD) and transfers to a novel station (0.96 SD, solve rate 63.6/70.6/83.3%).
agent_test: Equivalent: give agent distilled expert strategy notes; test on held-out novel systems at equal tokens.
audit_note: Numbers match, but Katz et al., the Gott et al. report and Parker are all the Sherlock developers' own evaluations (Katz summarises the same data as Gott), so there is no independent source.

claim: Tutoring on strategy (Hydrive) improved a verbal troubleshooting test; procedure-focused tutor and control did not (within-group pre/post t(19)=4.14).
agent_test: Strategy notes vs procedure notes in the prompt.
note: Gap search: Hydrive vs F-15 tutor differ in developer, CTA and content; within-group test only.

claim: ITBench found agents on 2024-era models resolved only 13.8% of SRE scenarios, ORCA-bench's best RCA accuracy was 25.3% on Medium and 10.0% on Hard tasks, and Cloud-OpsBench's best joint RCA accuracy was 0.76 (OnlineBoutique) and 0.68 (TrainTicket) but with evidence closure of only 0.38 and 0.15.
agent_test: Use as baseline difficulty; do not expect near-ceiling.
audit_note: Numbers are right, but Cloud-OpsBench's 0.76/0.68 is the best joint RCA accuracy (a high score, not a failure), and ITBench tested 2024-era models (GPT-4o, Llama) rather than strong current agents.
claim_before_audit: Strong LLM agents fail most realistic fault diagnosis: ITBench SRE 13.8%, ORCA-bench best 25.3% Medium / 10.0% Hard, Cloud-OpsBench joint accuracy 0.76/0.68.

claim: Final-answer scores overstate diagnosis: correct cause often has no grounded evidence path (OpenRCA 2.0: 76.0% right service but 61.5% grounded; Cloud-OpsBench evidence closure 0.38/0.15).
agent_test: Score evidence-closure, not only answer; add a require-supporting-evidence guard.
note: Gap search: OpenRCA 2.0 PR 61.5% vs AnySvc 76.0% confirmed; no one tests closure as a selection signal.

claim: Agents anchor on the first/loudest anomaly, like novices on surface features; noise lowers diagnosis (SREGym 72.6% to 62.6%).
agent_test: Inject a persistent decoy anomaly; compare with an 'enumerate other causes' step.
note: Gap search: SREGym trajectories confirm first-anomaly greed under injected noise; enumerate-alternatives at equal tokens still untested.
audit_note: SREGym drop is for Claude Code (Sonnet 4.6); the 'like novices' link is the researcher's analogy.

claim: Removing source code cut RCA accuracy by 9-16 points across models in ORCA-bench, and GALA+, a method that bounds exploration with the service dependency graph, reached 74.44% AC@1 on Online Boutique against 48.35% for the best prior LLM method (Flow-of-Action), though this compares whole systems and is not a dependency-graph ablation.
agent_test: Ablate system model access at equal tokens.
audit_note: ORCA 9-16 pts is right, but GALA+ 74.44% vs 48.35% compares a whole multi-phase system with a different published method (Flow-of-Action), not a with/without dependency-graph ablation.
claim_before_audit: Knowing the system (source code, dependency graph) is a lever: removing code cuts RCA 9-16 pts; a dependency graph raises AC@1 to 74% from 48%.

claim: Pattern-matched fixes can work without correct diagnosis (mitigation 22-62% after wrong diagnosis), but cost more attempts (3.82 vs 1.88, no-noise condition).
agent_test: Track repair success separately from diagnosis.

claim: Diagnosing well does not give repairing well: root-cause accuracy 91-99% but recovery validity 36.8-60.3%.
agent_test: Evaluate repair step separately.
note: Gap search: R2Act error taxonomy 67.9% wrong operation, 29.7% invalid plan structure, 1.3% wrong target; gold RCA + mapper only 0.599; live replay 48.3%. Cause is action validity/operation choice.

claim: On SREGym, end-to-end success of LLM SRE agents fell on its 13 new failure scenarios compared with ported problems (Stratus/Sonnet 4.6 63.7% to 17.9%, Claude Code 60.8% to 28.2%, Codex 57.8% to 15.4%), while similar-failure problems stayed near ported levels; this is one benchmark.
agent_test: Held-out novelty test: familiar vs new fault families.
audit_note: Only SREGym supports it (63.7% to 17.9% is Stratus/Sonnet 4.6, n=13 new-failure problems); the second source is a human transfer study that says nothing about LLM agents.
claim_before_audit: Performance collapses on novel failure types compared with familiar ones (SREGym E2E 63.7% to 17.9%).

claim: In OpsHarness, a harness that mines past diagnoses into knowledge, skills and tools reached 59.0% final A@1, against 38.4% for in-context retrieval of three correct past rollouts and 36.1% for the bare agent; in Trace2Policy only error-refined rules (78.9%) beat few-shot examples (73.3%), while one-shot distilled rules (69.2%) did not.
agent_test: Compare raw-trace retrieval vs distilled rule memory at equal tokens.
note: Gap search: OpsHarness is time-split on same systems with tools included; Trace2Policy shows unrefined distilled rules lowered strong models 7-9 pts vs zero-shot (non-diagnosis). Beats raw traces, not proven vs no text.
audit_note: OpsHarness numbers match, but Trace2Policy found one-shot distilled rules (69.2%) no better than no rules (70.3%) and worse than few-shot (73.3%); only error-refined rules (78.9%) won, and OpsHarness's 59.0% bundles knowledge, skills, tools and a cold-start substrate.
claim_before_audit: Distilled experience (rules, skills) beats raw retrieved cases: ICL of 3 past rollouts 38.4% vs Direct 36.1%; evolved harness 59.0%.

claim: Self-updating memory needs a held-out regression gate; without it accuracy fell (0.33 vs 0.43 no-evolve), 37% of proposals rejected.
agent_test: Memory write with and without verification gate.
note: Gap search: second independent source (Trace2Policy, 2% rollback gate; bypass fell to 66.8/67.5). Held-out sizes 40/139 are too small; testbed size in OpsHarness not stated.
audit_note: The no-verify ablation removes the whole verification gate (inner and outer), not the held-out gate alone; the 37% rejection rate is with the gate on.

claim: Open-ended adaptive investigation beats constrained pipelines/hand-built agents; backbone matters more than framework at the top.
agent_test: Keep scaffold light; compare free vs rigid procedure.

claim: More rounds do not help: failed runs ran up to 11.4 more rounds; more reasoning effort gives +2-4 pts at 1.5-4x time.
agent_test: Cap steps; compare accuracy per token.
audit_note: Lu's 'up to 11.4 more rounds' is a correlation between failure and length, not proof that extra rounds fail to help.

claim: A small rule-based guard against omitted/misread/unsupported evidence raised Acc@1 in all 14 configs (median +10.5 pts).
agent_test: Replicate guard on our agent.
note: Gap search: same median +10.5 reconfirmed; arms are not token-matched.

claim: In one large study (Zheng et al. 2024: 162 personas, 4 open LLM families, 2,410 factual MMLU questions) adding a persona, including expertise-domain roles, to the system prompt did not improve accuracy over no persona on average, and picking the best persona per question was about as good as random; domain-aligned roles helped only slightly.
agent_test: Persona prompt vs none at equal tokens: expect no gain.
note: Gap search: persona test covers 162 personas x 2,410 factual questions only; no diagnosis-specific test found.
audit_note: Only Zheng et al. (one paper, listed twice) tests it, on factual MMLU questions with open models, and finds small domain-alignment effects; Borchers et al. is about LLMs simulating novice students, not expert personas.
claim_before_audit: Telling an LLM to act as an expert does not raise accuracy; expert persona is not expertise.

claim: In a 15-participant study of embedded-system development and debugging, participants using GPT with a structured workflow scored 65.48 vs 34.21 without GPT (t(38)=2.73, p<0.01), with all five users on the environmental-sensor task scoring 100% (including some with no hardware experience) against 25% without GPT; the models also hallucinated hardware facts (e.g. wrong I2C address from pin voltage in 38% of trials, a wrong register or configuration value in 100%).
agent_test: Check domain-fact hallucination rate with and without grounded notes.
audit_note: The 65.48 vs 34.21 score is the mean over all 15 participants (students, faculty, professional engineers) on embedded development tasks, not novices only or debugging only; HypoCompass is software debugging and Hu and Ash is qualitative.
claim_before_audit: LLM help gives novices big gains in hardware debugging when structured (65.48 vs 34.21), but models hallucinate domain facts.

claim: LLM-generated tacit-knowledge guides from expert behaviour closed the expert-novice gap in a tutoring task.
agent_test: Distill expert traces to notes and test on held-out cases.
note: Gap search: Cho et al. Study 1 used GPT-4o as reader and Study 2 100 human novices per condition; tutoring task, not diagnosis.

claim: Chunking/pattern store: experts use large learned pattern libraries (chess 2895 Elo without search; Chase and Simon).
agent_test: Not opened for Chase and Simon; do not rely.
note: Gap search: primary papers blocked; only a secondary summary was read.

claim: In an exploratory Westermo case study (2 failure scenarios, 6 practitioners, 120 runs) neither the single-agent nor the orchestrated multi-agent RCA configuration showed a consistent practitioner-rated quality advantage, and the single agent was faster and cheaper.
agent_test: Single vs multi-agent at equal tokens.
audit_note: Westermo paper reports no consistent quality advantage (scenario-dependent) from 2 scenarios and 6 practitioners; Bi et al. compares simple harnesses with published agents, not single vs multi-agent.
claim_before_audit: Single agent matched multi-agent system in practitioner-rated quality and was cheaper.

claim: OpsHarness verifies each proposed memory or tool change with an inner gate (no accuracy or cost regression on the source cases) and an outer gate (no regression on a freshly re-sampled held-out testbed stratified by fault family and time); removing the whole gate made accuracy decay (final-window A@1 0.33 vs 0.43 for no-evolve) and hurt weak backbones most, but the two stages were not ablated separately; Trace2Policy independently found a regression gate necessary, in a different domain.
agent_test: Write memory with inner gate, outer gate, and no gate; track held-out accuracy over 12 windows. Use a testbed of several hundred cases, not 40-139.
audit_note: The two-stage design is described accurately, but only the whole gate was ablated (no stage-by-stage test), and the second source (Trace2Policy) uses a single validation regression gate in a different domain, so 'should pass a two-stage gate' is not shown.
claim_before_audit: Memory writes should pass a two-stage gate: no regression on the source cases and no regression on a fresh held-out set stratified by fault family. Without a gate accuracy decays and weak models overfit most.

claim: Distilled strategy artifacts beat raw retrieved traces at about equal tokens on later cases of the same systems (59.0 vs 38.4 vs 36.1), but a strategy-text-only arm and a novel-fault test do not exist, and unrefined distilled rules lowered strong models' accuracy in a non-diagnosis task.
agent_test: Arms: no text, raw traces, distilled strategy text, at equal tokens, on held-out novel fault families; include a strong and a weak model.

claim: The repair gap is mostly invalid operation and plan structure after a correct diagnosis, not missing diagnosis: 67.9% wrong operation, 29.7% invalid plan structure, 1.3% wrong target among 755 invalid plans; live replay recovers 48.3%.
agent_test: Add typed action space and precondition check before repair; compare recovery validity with and without it at equal tokens.

claim: Evidence closure (a verified causal path) exposes ungrounded correct answers (PR 61.5% vs AnySvc 76.0%) and reorders models (Qwen3.6-Max 91% vs Sonnet 4.6 66% conditional grounding), but no study shows it is a better training or selection signal than answer accuracy.
agent_test: Best-of-N with selection by closure vs by answer vote vs by confidence, at equal tokens.

claim: Gathering more evidence can make an agent drop a correct tool candidate: overrides outnumber corrections in every configuration; verifying with raw metrics helps (corrections 2.7% to 5.3%), adding competing analysis hurts (overrides 9.3%).
agent_test: Default to the recalled rule; allow override only after a named conflict check on raw evidence; measure override vs correction counts.

claim: No component ablation of Sherlock-style tutoring exists, and the only comparison (Hydrive vs F-15 tutor) mixes developer, task-analysis method and content; Sherlock samples are 12-23 per cell from the developers' lab with no independent replication found.
agent_test: Three-arm agent test: system model only, strategy list only, verify-before-act only.

claim: Persona effect on diagnosis tasks is untested; the only systematic test is factual QA (162 personas, 2,410 questions, no gain).
agent_test: Persona vs none on a fault-diagnosis set at equal tokens.

claim: Chase and Simon 1973 and Chi et al. 1981 were blocked by publishers and remain unopened; the pattern-store advantage on fault cases and its loss on novel cases are not measured.
agent_test: Not testable from literature in hand; test directly with familiar vs novel fault families.
